approachQuestion.prompt:
Replace a Docket Section

A finite acyclic singly linked list has n nodes. Given zero-based positions a and b, remove inclusive positions a..b and put a second list in their place. The second list is disjoint, nonempty, finite and acyclic, and both its head and tail are supplied. Return the new head, preserving every survivor and replacement node, value and relative order. Change only next links. Removed nodes need not be cleared. Constraints: 0 <= a <= b < n <= 200000; replacement length m satisfies 1 <= m <= 200000. Only the first list's head is supplied, not its length or tail.

Input: first A -> B -> C -> D -> E, a=1,b=3; replacement X -> Y, with head X and tail Y. Output: A -> X -> Y -> E -> null.
Input: first A, a=b=0; replacement X. Output: X -> null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Walk from a temporary sentinel to find the node before a and the successor of b. Link that predecessor to the replacement head, link the supplied replacement tail to the saved successor, and return sentinel.next.
options.feedback: Only the removed range boundaries are needed; the supplied replacement tail avoids traversing the inserted chain.

options.text: Collect all first-list references in an array, then use indices a and b to connect the same boundaries to the supplied replacement head and tail.
options.feedback: This performs the correct splice but scans and stores the whole first list even when the replaced prefix is short.

options.text: Link the predecessor of a to replacement head and replacement tail to the original node at b.
options.feedback: The inclusive endpoint b remains. For first [A,B,C], a=b=1 and replacement X, this yields A,X,B,C instead of A,X,C.

options.text: Attach replacement head after the predecessor of a but leave replacement tail.next unchanged.
options.feedback: For [A,B,C], a=b=1 and a null-terminated X, this loses surviving C.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-16-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here b is the inclusive zero-based end position in the first list; m is the replacement length. The replacement tail is supplied. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: Finding the successor of b from head takes b+1 advances; finding the predecessor of a adds at most b+1, followed by fixed link writes. No walk through m replacement nodes is needed because its tail is supplied. A sentinel and fixed references are constant storage; output reuses nodes.
